Variants.Content: Dorne recognizes that the eldest daughter has the same inheritance qualifications as the eldest son, which makes its family structure significantly different from that of the other seven kingdoms. The Dornish people regard this as a natural legal system, and foreign nobles sometimes have difficulty adapting; differences in inherited customs can become a real force in marriage alliances and diplomacy.

Entry Dornish Eldest-Child Inheritance Dorne recognizes that the eldest daughter has the same inheritance qualifications as the eldest son, which makes its family structure significantly different from that of the other seven kingdoms. The Dornish people regard this as a natural legal system, and foreign nobles sometimes have difficulty adapting; differences in inherited customs can become a real force in marriage alliances and diplomacy. Whether it is valid depends on who can grant the rights, collect the consideration, and actually make the judgment come to fruition in the event of default.
